entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard, learned counsel for the parties.

1. The order dated 15.10.2022 of maintenance passed by learned Principal Judge, Family Court,
Godda, in O. M. C. No.161 of 2019 under Section 125 Cr. P.C. whereby and whereunder maintenance of Rs.10,000/- per month has been imposed is under-challenge in the instant Criminal Revision.

2. The impugned order has been challenged on two grounds :- firstly the Opp. Party No.2 was not a legally married wife of the petitioner and secondly, the quantum of maintenance is highly excessive and not supported by any evidence of income of petitioner.
3.
As per the case of the applicant/ Opp. Party No.2, she was married to the petitioner in the year 2004 and had normal matrimonial life for two years.
Thereafter she was subjected to cruelty in reference to unlawful demand and due to assault, her pregnancy suffered miscarriage.
She was ousted from her matrimonial home on 22.08.2007 and consequently she filed a case under Section 498A IPC and other Sections.

4. On the point of income of the petitioner, it has been asserted that he was having a workshop for making Mixture and snacks in Pakur, from which he has annual income of Rs.20 Lakhs and also has a mango orchard from which he Rs.5 Lakhs per annum.
On considering the evidence, the learned court below has awarded maintenance of Rs.10,000/- per month.

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that no material has been brought on record to show that he was an Income Tax payee or GST was paid for the production of the food products as asserted in the maintenance case.
The applicant herself has deposed to the Court's question that she cannot give definite account of the income of the petitioner.
The main contention of the petitioner is that without any credible evidence, the maintenance amount has been awarded which is highly excessive.
6. Learned APP for the State has defended the impugned order.

It is submitted that altogether four witnesses have been examined on behalf of the applicant and all of them have consistently stated that the petitioner was in the business of Tobacco as well as in that of food product like mixture and snacks.
7. Heard the submissions advanced on behalf of both the sides and perused the materials on record.
There is some merit in the submission advanced on behalf of the petitioner that his business has been exaggerated and excess income has been assessed by the learned court below.
There is no evidence regarding the place of the factory, or any documentary evidence regarding taxes, or electricity bill paid by the said unit.

What can be conjured from the oral testimony of the witnesses is that the petitioner was doing small time business of selling food products and at the same time was supplementing his income by selling tobacco.
From the nature of the business and the place where it was located claim of income of Rs.20 Lakhs per annum was highly excessive and disproportionate.

Had it been the income of Rs 20 lakhs, a maintenance of only Rs 15000/- would not have been sought for.
8.
In absence of any documentary evidence regarding the said factory and the income accruing therefrom, a maintenance of Rs.5,000/- per month to the Opp. Party No.2 shall be just and reasonable.
Under the circumstances, the instant Criminal Revision is disposed of with modification of the maintenance amount to be paid to the Opp. Party No.2.

(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) Sandeep/ Uploaded.
